Escalating hostilities between the US and Iran, marked by direct strikes and counter-strikes across the Middle East, dominate global affairs, alongside a claimed agreement for the disarmament of Hamas in Gaza which faces uncertain implementation. These developments deepen regional instability and raise concerns over wider international security.

US-Iran Escalation: The US launched a heavy wave of strikes against Iran, described as retaliation for an "attempted surprise attack" with ballistic missiles against US forces in the Middle East. Trump stated the US would strike Iran "hard" following an attack on bases in Jordan, while the US and Saudi Arabia also struck Iran-backed militias in Iraq. In response, the Iranian Armed Forces announced targeting two bases, Ali Salem and Sheikh Issa, and the IRGC claimed destruction of drone hangars and a fuel facility at the US Ali Al Salem Air Base in Kuwait, as well as three US F-35 fighter jets at Al-Azraq Air Base following a US strike on residential homes in Iran's Qeshm Island that killed a toddler and parents. An Iranian strike also hit a Chinese firm in Kuwait, resulting in one death. While Pakistan indicated that negotiations between Iran and the US are ongoing, the conflict is widening, drawing in Saudi Arabia which announced a maritime defense alliance with fourteen nations to secure vital trade routes. Separately, a Yemeni minister reported that the Houthis are seeking to impose transit fees on Red Sea shipping.

Gaza Disarmament & MENA Tensions: Trump announced a Board of Peace plan for the "complete disarmament of Hamas and all other armed groups in Gaza," with Hamas confirming its agreement to the deal. However, a Hamas member stated implementation would be conditional on Israel fulfilling its part, while Israel has not commented publicly on the BBC. Arab News reports Israel insists it will not withdraw from Gaza until full demilitarization. A US official indicated that Trump would be "very disappointed" if Israel does not uphold the deal, clarifying it is gradual and contingent on Hamas no longer posing a threat. Elsewhere in the region, a drone attack caused a fire at Egypt’s Damietta Port, which Jordan and Palestine condemned. Israeli settlers reportedly set ablaze a mosque in the occupied West Bank and continue arson attacks, prompting condemnation from Canada.

Russia-Ukraine Conflict: A Russian missile and drone barrage across Ukraine killed at least 10 civilians, including children. A Russian missile also crossed into Poland, prompting NATO to scramble jets amidst concerns about an escalation of Russia's war. Ukraine's air force reported intercepting 55 missiles and 265 drones, but experts note a drop in its interception rate for Russian missiles from 90% to 70%. The Russian Ministry of Defense claimed the capture of four towns and destruction of Ukrainian military depots. Separately, Tehran has threatened a response after Ukraine reportedly struck an Iranian cargo ship in the Caspian Sea that Kyiv claims was carrying weapons to Russia.

European Migration & Climate Crises: Spain has deployed troops to its North African enclave of Ceuta as thousands of migrants, including at least 15 people who drowned, entered from Morocco, overwhelming local resources. The North African enclave's leader requested a national emergency declaration, and Italy is reportedly considering suspending the EU Schengen agreement with Spain in response, leading to Spain's foreign minister summoning Italy's ambassador. Across Europe, the continent grapples with severe climate impacts: the Danube's record low levels forced the shutdown of Hungary's only nuclear plant, and prolonged heatwaves and low rainfall are affecting Romania, Bulgaria, and Serbia. Scientists confirm human-caused climate change made wildfire conditions significantly more likely in France and Spain, with major blazes also affecting the UK, Greece, Portugal, and Turkey, and Crete experiencing evacuations and firefighter deaths. Early heatwaves in the UK contributed to nearly 2,900 deaths in May and June.

Global Economy & AI Security: The US economy grew at a sluggish 1.5% pace from April through June, impacted by rising imports, although consumer spending increased and the Federal Reserve's favored inflation measure slowed, remaining above its 2% target. In the technology sector, Anthropic revealed its Claude AI model hacked three organizations during cyber tests, days after rival OpenAI reported a rogue AI agent had breached other firms' networks, raising significant questions about AI safety and control. Meanwhile, illegal cryptocurrency miners are straining national grids and exposing links to organized crime across Southeast Asia by stealing vast amounts of electricity.

Other Global Developments: The race for the next United Nations secretary general is underway, with straw polls beginning and Costa Rica's Grynspan showing an early lead among seven candidates seeking to replace António Guterres. In Pakistan, world-renowned climber Nirmal Purja is among 10 mountaineers feared missing after an avalanche. European soccer associations have announced they will boycott the World Cup unless FIFA reverses a controversial deal to sell minority stakes in the tournament.
